newsitem.title: UK: American Air says settled dispute with SW Trains.
newsitem.headline: American Air says settled dispute with SW Trains.

text.p: American Airlines said Tuesday it had an agreement in principle with Britain's Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains after earlier filing a suit over the rail company's use of the "Advantage" name.
An American Airlines spokeswoman refused to comment further on the matter.
Sources said American filed a suit against Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains over the rail company's use of the "Advantage" name in some of its brochures.
American Airlines uses "Advantage" as the name of its frequent flyer programme.
Earlier, a spokeswoman for SW Trains said it was aware of the suit and added that the two parties had "reached an agreement in principle. But it is not finalised."
